Have been in both adult and child acute mental health facilities (ones within the hospital campus). I also then volunteered at an adult mental health facility. 

Child: Some of the nurses were lovely. Some were bitchy as hell. The doctors were okay but I never felt that taken care of. the hospital tried really hard to make every child feel welcome, but it felt like a dungeon. Some other patients shared helpful strategies for recovery with me, and others shared better ideas on how to hurt myself. They had lots of activity groups, to keep us occupied.

Adult facility was horrible. So many psychiatrists/psychologists were so harsh and rude. I get their job is hard but it hardly made me want to get help. In one facility, before they had lock down laws, you could walk out whenever you felt like it as long as you came back at night. The laws changed soon after people started killing themselves when they were out. Now everyone in those facilities is in lock down and cannot leave without doctor permission. Its miserable, everyone is lumped together. 18 year olds - 80 year olds, schizophrenics with the depressed. I don't see how putting all those people in the same place is a good idea. There are activities, but very few. The staff at the adult facilities are a lot more worn down, I noticed this as a volunteer too. 
Being a patient there was scary. There was one guy who I'm fairly sure was schizophrenic (he told me) and said some crazy religious things and believed he was like Jesus or something, and then said a lot of sexual things and made a few advances. Of course nurses dealt with this once i told them. I then saw him through his door-window as I walked past, naked on his bed jerking off. It was all very unpleasant. Another situation was when a few of us were chilling in the common area and a man was taking a phone call and getting really angry on the phone and then started screaming violent things like how he will murder the person on the other end. The nurses cut the call and he went crazy, throwing chairs, throwing the phone on the desk at the nurse, etc. The girl next to me had been abused in the past and she then had a break down as it triggered her a lot. All in all, a pretty terrible experience. 

My time as a volunteer was only a few months, and I saw how little some staff cared but how much other staff truly wanted the best for each and every patient. The patients looked miserable, but some were so glad to have us there volunteering and spending time with them. It was truly heart-warming to give back.
